To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the network model of the CA3 region of the hippocampus can simulate the effects of scopolmine on human free recall and recognition, and that these effects are due to the selective impairment of encoding of new items, and the selective sparing of retrieval of previously encoded items.

the network model simulates the effects of the muscarinic cholinergic blocker scopolamine to impair human delayed free recall but not delayed recognition of words presented in a word recognition experiment, and that this impairment is due to the scopolamine-induced weakening of recurrent connections in the CA3 region of the hippocampus.
the hippocampal network model can simulate the effects of scopolamide on human memory function, and can account for the asymmetries of the scopolamide effect on human free recall and recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
modeling the role of the hippocampus in memory function.
the role of the hippocampus in human memory, and how this role is affected by the cholinergic system.
the development of a network model of hippocampal function, with a focus on modeling the effect of acetylcholinergic blockade on memory function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
scopolamine impairs free recall of items learned under the influence of the drug but does not impair recognition of those items.

the network model of the CA3 region of the hippocampus, with the addition of cholinergic inputs, can replicate the memory impairments seen with scopolamine in humans and also provides an explanation of the mechanisms of action of scopolamine in the brain.
the model is able to replicate a wide range of data from human subjects, including the effects of scopolaming on free recall, recognition, and the list-strength and proactive interference effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scopolamine blocks the formation of attractor states for items but not context.
scopolamine selectively blocks the strengthening of new associations in the hippocampus, but allows retrieval of previously stored associations to occur.
scopolamine impairs free recall by selectively impairing the encoding of new information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple network model can account for the effects of scopolamide on memory, but that the model is sensitive to the details of the experimental paradigm.
a network model of hippocampal function, incorporating simplified simulations at the neuronal level, can simulate many of the behavioral effects of scopolmine on human memory.

a simple network model incorporating simplified simulations of the cellular effects and network connectivity of the hippocampus can account for a range of human memory phenomena, and that this model provides an account of the effects of scopolamide on human memory that is consistent with the cellular effects of this drug.
